source.title: Performance-Efficiency Trade-Offs in Adapting Language Models to Text Classification Tasks
source.authors: Laura Aina; Nikos Voskarides; Roi Blanco

record.file_problem: No apparent garbling or cutoff; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study varies model size and training-set size and measures downstream classification accuracy, bearing on V6, but it does not measure pretraining loss or fit scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The study reports downstream classification accuracy under different model sizes, training-set sizes, and adaptation procedures. It does not test power-law loss, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, or isolated architecture effects. Detailed appendix plot cells are not individually recorded because their flattened layout does not reliably associate every value with its condition.
record.test_reason: The study compares five pretrained BERT sizes (11M–336M) on downstream classification accuracy across labeled-set sizes. This bears on V6 in a new setting (fine-tuning and prompt-tuning). It fits no laws and measures no pretraining loss, so V1–V5 and V7 are untouched.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors find fine-tuning and prompting work well for large LMs on large train sets, but cheaper alternatives exist. P+KD reduces compute and data cost at once, and adaptation choices should follow compute and labeling budgets.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates adaptation of pretrained BERT models for classification, measuring test accuracy while varying model and labeled train-set sizes. It does not reproduce pretraining-loss scaling measurements or fit scaling laws.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported accuracy varies with training-set size, model size, adaptation procedure, and KD teacher exposure; the hyperparameter search is generalized across some model and data configurations.

fits_no_version.finding: Knowledge distillation and prompting change downstream accuracy more than model size does in low-data regimes; a distilled 11M model matches the 335M teacher below 320 examples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The training/adaptation procedure can substitute for model scale on downstream classification in low-data regimes.

fits_no_version.finding: Downstream accuracy rises with labeled fine-tuning set size, and gaps between procedures shrink as the set grows.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream accuracy scales with fine-tuning data size across adaptation procedures.

record.problems: The paper focuses on four English classification datasets and inference efficiency rather than training compute. It selects the best of four runs by dev accuracy for its main comparisons, and it simplifies/generalizes some hyperparameter-search choices across configurations. Some detailed plot values in the supplied text are flattened and cannot be reliably assigned to every model-condition cell.
record.rows_left_out: Individual accuracy and standard-deviation cells in Figures 2 and 3, and the full hyperparameter entries in Table 3, were not extracted because the supplied flattened layouts do not reliably preserve all cell-to-condition assignments; the aggregate trends and recommendations are recorded in r2–r5.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss and no power-law fits.
Shape is not varied at fixed parameter count.
No power-law fits in fine-tuning or other regimes.
No relation to pretraining loss, no fitted or predictive relationship, and the scale range is narrow (11M–336M, five models).
No fitted exponents or comparison of fitting choices.

missing.what: Accuracy by model size at large train sets for fine-tuning and prompting (monotonic increase, e.g. Yahoo F 20480: 0.68, 0.70, 0.70, 0.72, 0.73).
Non-monotonic size effects with high variance at 20–160 examples under fine-tuning (e.g. AG News at 20: 0.27/0.5/0.46/0.56/0.37).

record.verdict_notes: This is weak evidence for V6. There are only five sizes, the models come from Turc et al. rather than a controlled scaling run, and results are the best of four runs chosen on dev sets. Depth and width also vary together. Of the existing rows, only r1 bears on V6. The size trend at large data lives in Figure 3 values that no row captures.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss and its power-law relation to parameters, tokens, or compute.
No scaling-law fits or predictions of much larger runs.
No fixed-compute comparison or fitted parameter/token allocation trend.
The models differ in depth, width, and attention heads, but the study does not isolate or quantify architecture effects at a fixed parameter count.
No other modalities or the listed alternative training regimes are tested.

Does not relate downstream results to pretraining loss or establish a fitted predictive relationship; tests classification accuracy across model and training-set sizes in the reported adaptation settings.
No fitted scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal split, and no comparison of scaling-law fitting choices.

rows.subject: BERT-large vs BERT 41.4M
rows.stage_stated: Pre-trained LMs adapted to text classification by fine-tuning
rows.operation_detail: Compared classification accuracy across model sizes and training-set sizes.
rows.note: The authors state that using more parameters is not always beneficial on very small training sets.
rows.check: Linked correctly. BERT-large is worse than BERT 41.4M on Yelp-full with fewer than 160 examples. The authors attribute this partly to initialization sensitivity and tiny dev sets.

rows.subject: BERT models across the five tested sizes
rows.stage_stated: Pre-trained LMs adapted to text classification by fine-tuning, prompting, or either procedure followed by KD
rows.operation_detail: Compared classification accuracy across training-set sizes and adaptation procedures.

conditions.value: Yelp-full, Yelp-polarity, Yahoo-questions, and AG News

rows.value: The authors report that accuracy increases as the train set grows and that differences between training procedures gradually shrink.
rows.note: This is an aggregate qualitative report across the studied datasets and configurations, not a reported fitted predictive relationship.
rows.check: The row is about labeled fine-tuning set size and gaps between procedures, not model or pretraining scale. It does not measure V6's effect.

source_check.locator_found: Sections 2.1 and 2.4; Table 1; Section 3.1, summary and Prompting.

rows.subject: BERT 11M and BERT 335.1M
rows.size_stated: 11M and 335.1M parameters; the smaller model is reported as having 30x fewer parameters and 7x faster inference
rows.stage_stated: Pre-trained LMs adapted by prompting followed by KD
rows.operation_detail: Compared the compact student with the large teacher across training-set sizes.
rows.value: BERT 11M performs comparably to BERT 335.1M for small train sets (<320)
rows.note: The reported result is comparability after a change in training procedure, not a monotonic size-only effect.
rows.check: The row compares a distilled (P+KD) student with its teacher, which is an effect of the procedure, not of scale. It should not be linked to V6.

source_check.problem: The comparison changes adaptation procedure as well as size; it should remain excluded from evidence for a size-only scaling effect.

rows.subject: Compact BERT student models
rows.size_stated: BERT-mini through BERT-base; sizes listed in Table 1
rows.stage_stated: Pre-trained LMs adapted to text classification; KD students trained from fine-tuned or prompted teachers
rows.operation_detail: Compared compact-model accuracy with and without distillation across training-set sizes.

conditions.value: KD benefit reported unless the teacher has more than 10240 examples; the section summary says unless the train set is larger than 2560

rows.value: KD generally increases the quality of compact models; larger student models tend to close more of the gap with the teacher
rows.locator: Section 3.1, Effect of Training Procedure; Figures 1–2
rows.note: The paper gives different thresholds in its summary and discussion: >2560 in the summary bullet and >10240 for the teacher in the detailed discussion. The result depends on training procedure and data availability, not scale alone.
rows.check: The main measure is KD versus no KD, an effect of the procedure. The side remark that larger students close more of the gap is a weak size trend under KD only.

source_check.locator_found: Section 3.1, summary bullets and KD paragraph.
source_check.problem: The principal comparison concerns KD versus no KD, rather than a scaling effect; the two reported training-set thresholds are accurately preserved.

relationships.condition: Fine-tuning or prompting with medium-to-large labeled sets (about 640+ examples), all four tasks
relationships.reason: Based on the text and the Figure 3 values, not on any row. Accuracy rises monotonically with model size, e.g. Yahoo fine-tuning at 20480 goes 0.68→0.73 and Yelp-full 0.57→0.63. The authors say bigger models perform better with more data.
relationships.display_finding: At 20,480 examples, fine-tuning accuracy increased 0.68→0.73 on Yahoo and 0.57→0.63 on Yelp-full, but at 640 examples larger models reduced Yelp-full fine-tuning accuracy 0.51→0.47 and Yahoo prompting accuracy 0.65→0.64.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Fine-tuning or prompting with medium-to-large labeled sets (about 640+ examples), all four tasks
source_check.reason: The cited 20480-example endpoints are correct, but improvement is not monotonic throughout this condition group. Figure 3 shows Yelp-full fine-tuning at 640 examples falling from 0.51 for BERT 109.5M to 0.47 for BERT 335.1M; Yahoo prompting at 640 also falls from 0.65 to 0.64 for the two largest models. Broadly positive trends coexist with exceptions. These model-size results need dedicated rows.

relationships.condition: Few-shot fine-tuning (fewer than about 320 labeled examples)
relationships.reason: Model-size gains are non-monotonic here. BERT-large underperforms BERT 41.4M on Yelp-full (r1). In the Figure 3 values, AG News at 20 examples goes 0.27/0.5/0.46/0.56/0.37, with large run-to-run variance.
relationships.display_finding: BERT-large underperformed BERT 41.4M on Yelp-full, while AG News scores with 20 examples varied non-monotonically across sizes at 0.27/0.50/0.46/0.56/0.37 with large run-to-run variance.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Few-shot fine-tuning (fewer than about 320 labeled examples)
source_check.reason: Few-shot results vary across models and datasets, qualifying a general improvement-with-size claim. Row r1 explicitly records worse Yelp-full performance for the larger model below 160 examples. Figure 3 confirms the cited non-monotonic AG News accuracies at 20 examples. The narrower reversed comparison in r1 can also justify challenges for that specific condition.

reader_labels.condition: Small training sets and changes in model size or adaptation procedure
reader_labels.reason: The size trend is not uniform: BERT-large can underperform a smaller model on Yelp-full with fewer than 160 examples (r1), while a prompted and distilled 11M model can match the large teacher below 320 examples (r3).
